findings.title: Unexpected exceptions abort the cutover without writing the report
findings.description:
`run_steps` catches only `(StepFailed, subprocess.CalledProcessError)`, but several step bodies can raise other exception types that are not converted to `StepFailed`:

- `step_production` (scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:243) does `(ctx.main.backup_root / "backup-health.log").read_text().splitlines()[-1]` with no guard — a missing log raises `FileNotFoundError`, an empty one raises `IndexError`.
- `step_weekly` (scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:180) does `log.read_text().splitlines()[-1] if log.exists() else ""` — an existing-but-empty `base.log` raises `IndexError`.

Either exception escapes `run_steps`, propagates out of `main()`, and the script dies with a traceback **without writing the report** — exactly the outcome the module docstring and TD8 promise against ("the first failure stops the run and the report is still written"). The same applies to `main()`'s pre-step calls: `cluster(TABLE_PATH, MAIN)` can raise `KeyError`, and `env_value` can raise `CalledProcessError`, both uncaught.

Note that `run_health` and `step_weekly` already guard the *existence* of their log files; the inconsistency between the guarded and unguarded reads is what makes the gap easy to miss. Catching `Exception` at the step boundary (recording it as the step's failure and continuing to the report write) would restore the documented contract.

findings.title: The replication host is defined in the table but hard-coded again in the cutover helper
findings.description:
`deploy/backup-clusters.conf` is the single source for `replication_host` (`127.0.0.1` for `17/main`), and `BackupCluster.replication_host` already carries it into the cutover's `Context`. But `strip_new_args` hard-codes the literal:

```python
line = line.replace(" --replication-host 127.0.0.1", "")
```

and `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` hard-codes a third copy in `_NEW_MAIN_ARGS`. AGENTS.md is explicit: "If a value is used in conditionals, switch cases, or lookups, define it once … Changing a value should require editing exactly one place."

The failure mode is fail-safe but confusing: if the table's `replication_host` changes, `strip_new_args` stops stripping the new argument, `production_changes` reports a spurious production-line change, and `step_apply` aborts the cutover with a diff that looks like a real production regression. Passing `ctx.main.replication_host` into `strip_new_args`/`production_changes` would make the comparison track the table automatically.

findings.title: The sudoers file no longer enumerates the commands the cutover issues
findings.description: The file's header states it holds "Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider … add a line when deploy/systemd gains a unit", and its `MT_UNITS` alias lists specific systemd units. The new cutover issues five root commands — `sudo -u postgres env PGCLUSTER=… psql`, `sudo sha256sum …`, `sudo deploy/setup-backup.sh …`, `sudo scripts/provision_tick_cluster.sh`, and `sudo systemctl restart postgresql@17-tick` — and none of them appear in `manta-ops`. The cutover will therefore prompt for an interactive sudo password at every root step (or fail outright if the operator has no general sudo), which the design's "one PM-run `sudo` session" wording glosses over. Either the needed entries are added, or the design states plainly that the PM types the password for these steps.

findings.title: The failure line of the per-cluster `pg_settings.sh` run names `env`, not the library
findings.description:
`run_lib` shifts the prefix off and then reports `basename "$1"` — but the only call that does not pass the library path first is the per-cluster PostgreSQL settings call:

```bash
run_lib "$C" env PGCLUSTER="$C" "$LIB_DIR/pg_settings.sh" "${CHECK_FLAG[@]}" "${PG_AS_USER[@]}" ...
```

After the `shift`, `$1` is `env`, so the failure line reads `MISSING 17/tick env exited 1` instead of naming `pg_settings.sh`. The `timeshift_merge.sh` and `restic_repo.sh` calls pass the library path first and are unaffected. This line is what an operator sees when a cluster's settings fail, so it should name the library.

findings.title: The block-termination convention is coupled to the current template layout
findings.description: `block_lines` ends a cluster block at the first line beginning with `#`. In the rendered file the tick block is terminated by the host template's `# host: system backup (restic), once per host` comment, so the cutover's parse of "the tick block" silently depends on the host template's comment placement. Separately, `render_cron.sh` drops only lines starting with `##`, so a single-`#` comment added to `deploy/cron.d/manta-trading-backup.cluster` as a template comment would be rendered verbatim into `/etc/cron.d/manta-trading-backup` **and** truncate the block the cutover parses (`block_commands` would then raise "lacks jobs"). The `##` convention is documented in the template header but nothing enforces it; a guard in `render_cron.sh` that rejects any unrecognised `#` line in the cluster template would make the convention self-enforcing rather than advisory.

findings.title: Production host facts are hard-coded in two test modules
findings.description: `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` defines `_PROD_CHECKOUT = "/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data"` and `_PROD_BUCKET = "b2:manta.trading.data"`, and `test/unit/test_cutover_227.py` defines its own `CHECKOUT` and `BUCKET` constants with the same values. Two copies of the same production facts mean a change to the checkout path or bucket name must be made in two files, and a mismatch between them would surface as an opaque diff in the production-equivalence comparison rather than as a naming error. A shared fixture or a single constants module would remove the duplication.

findings.title: The new scripts sit outside the configured type-checking scope
findings.description: `[tool.mypy]` sets `files = ["src/manta_trading"]`, so `scripts/cutover_227_helpers.py`, `scripts/cutover_227_host.py` and `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py` are not covered by the configured run, and the repository's only GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) is a tag-triggered publish job with no lint or test step. The slice's Technical Requirements call for "ruff, mypy and shellcheck (-x) clean on touched files", but nothing in the configuration mechanically enforces it for these files. The `[tool.ruff.lint]` block does satisfy the required select list (`E`, `F`, `W`, `I`, `UP`, `BLE`, `ASYNC`, `B`), and the new files' imports and formatting are consistent with it — the gap is only that the check is opt-in rather than configured.

findings.title: Production's cron lines are protected by a two-sided equivalence check
findings.description: The render refuses a template without an exact `@CLUSTER_BLOCKS@` line, refuses unfilled `@NAME@` placeholders across both templates, and refuses an unescaped `%` before anything can reach `/etc/cron.d`. The production-equivalence contract (TD3) is enforced independently in two places: `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py::test_production_lines_gain_only_the_new_arguments` compares the stripped rendered main block and host block against the real pre-227 fixture line for line, and `cutover_227_helpers.production_changes` applies the same comparison to the file the cutover actually installs. The `--replication-host` duplication noted above is the one place where that equivalence depends on a value that is not read from the table.

findings.title: The B2 lifecycle path is read-only and the destructive alternative is documented
findings.description: `b2_lifecycle.sh` reads the rules through rclone's native `:b2:` backend and never sets one, with the rclone v1.75.0 `b2_update_bucket` behaviour (which replaces every rule with one whole-bucket rule) documented in the header so a future maintainer does not "fix" the gap by adding a write path. The rule's non-fatal status is implemented coherently across both languages: `setup-backup.sh` prints the missing rule with `echo` rather than `report`, so it never enters the `not-ok` tally, and `cutover_227_helpers.setup_not_ok` excludes the same line shape with `^MISSING \S+ lifecycle ` — a shape that deliberately does *not* match the `lifecycle-read` line, so an unreadable rule set still fails the cutover. `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py::test_never_sets_a_rule` asserts that every rclone invocation is `backend lifecycle` with no write flags, and `test_missing_rule_does_not_change_the_exit_code` pins the exit-code invariance.
